summary: This is a reusable Bash library for drawing a progress bar. You source it into another script, then pipe output containing "Progress=N" lines through the `progress_bar::process` function, which reads those lines, extracts the progress number, and draws an animated bar showing how far you've gotten.

explanations.48: This tells Bash to immediately exit if you use a variable that was never set, preventing silent bugs from undefined names.
explanations.49: This tells Bash to immediately exit if any command fails, so errors don't get silently ignored and the script keeps running.
explanations.52: This is an array with two special characters: a filled block (█) for the completed portion of the bar and a lighter block (▒) for the remaining portion.
explanations.74: This prints spaces equal to the terminal width to stderr, which effectively clears the current line so the progress bar can redraw on top of itself.
explanations.76: This command asks the terminal how many columns (characters wide) it currently is, then stores that number so the progress bar knows how much space it has.
explanations.88: The `?` syntax means this parameter is required; if someone calls the function without passing `progress`, Bash will error with the message "progress is mandatory".
explanations.90: The `:-` syntax provides a default value; if the caller doesn't pass `info`, it defaults to "In progress".
explanations.99: The `printf -v` syntax means "instead of printing, store the result in the variable `info_segment`", allowing us to build up the text before displaying it.
explanations.103: This calculates what percentage of the total work is done by multiplying progress by 100 and dividing by total.
explanations.114: This creates a string of spaces whose length equals `progress_segment_size`; we'll later replace those spaces with the filled block character to show the completed portion.
explanations.119: The `${var//pattern/replacement}` syntax replaces all spaces in `progress_segment` with the filled block character (█), creating the visual "done" part of the bar.
explanations.157: This loop reads one line at a time from whatever is piped in, waiting for input continuously (not all at once).
explanations.159: This regex looks for the pattern "Progress=" followed by one or more digits, capturing just the digits in a special variable called `BASH_REMATCH[1]`.
explanations.167: This tries to return from the script (which works when sourced) and uses the exit code to detect whether we're being sourced (return succeeds) or run directly (return fails).
explanations.169: This prints an error message in bold red to stderr, telling the user they must use `source` instead of running the script directly.
